attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as an Ansible-managed DHCP server on the private network it shares with node2/node3 (eth1/enp8s0, 10.50.50.0/24), and configured node2/node3 (RHEL 10) via Ansible to obtain their address on that network via DHCP instead of static assignment. Automation runs from node4, the cluster's designated control node (pre-provisioned with ansible-core and its own SSH keypair). Built an inventory (dhcp_server group using vyos.vyos/network_cli, dhcp_clients group using standard SSH) and a playbook that: (1) applies `vyos.vyos.vyos_config` lines to set eth1's address and a Kea-backed `service dhcp-server` shared-network/subnet/range/default-router/lease on node1, committed and saved; (2) uses `community.general.nmcli` to set enp8s0's connection to ipv4 method=auto (DHCP) on node2/node3, brings it up, and waits for a leased address. Playbook run is idempotent (second run reports changed=0 on node1). Verified node2 got 10.50.50.100/24 and node3 got 10.50.50.101/24 from node1's Kea DHCP server, with correct routes and gateway. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured baseline boot_id and health on all four nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time (never concurrently), confirmed each acquired a new boot_id, and confirmed post-restart recovery — node1's DHCP service and persisted lease file survived; node2 and node3 automatically reacquired their same DHCP leases on boot; node4's ansible-playbook re-run against the recovered fleet still succeeds end-to-end.
